doc: Zonal means of continentality (300 km smoothing) and of deck_window x deck_strength in the 15 bands x in [k/6, (k+1)/6) of x = |lat| / phi_H (both hemispheres together; a row with x >= 15/6 is in no band). Float32 field means in float32: default tolerance, measured worst difference against the float64 chain 2.2e-8. The coast threshold is at least 1e-4 from every texel (asserted). THE HALF-OPEN BANDS [a, b) PINNED AT THEIR EDGES: 72x36 synthetic world (rows every 5 degrees), Hadley 45, Earth radius, prograde. Seven rows have x EXACTLY equal to an edge k/6 in float64: row 1 (edge 11, x = 11/6), row 4 (edge 9, x = 9/6), row 7 (edge 7, x = 7/6), row 10 (edge 5, x = 5/6), row 13 (edge 3, x = 3/6), row 22 (edge 3, x = 3/6), row 31 (edge 9, x = 9/6) (rows counted from the north; rows 13 and 22 are the two hemispheres at 22.5 degrees, row 31 is the mirror of row 4; x is |lat|, both hemispheres land in the same bands). A tie row belongs to the band that STARTS at its edge (x >= a) and not to the one that ends there (x < b). A comparison written `x > a` drops these rows from every band, and `x <= b` counts them twice: both change the band means by up to 0.076 (continentality) and 0.023 (deck) on this world (measured by mutating the comparison in a scratch copy). 5 other rows lie within 1e-9 of an edge without being equal to it (rows 16, 19, 25, 28, 34): they fall on the side float64 rounding puts them, which is why the output `row_x` (|degrees(lat)| / hadley of every row, computed with the numpy degrees = x * (180 / pi), lat = pi / 2 - (i + 0.5) pi / h) is an output compared EXACTLY: a port whose row_x differs in the last bit puts some rows in the neighboring band, and this case is then to be read with that difference in mind, not as a failure of the band logic. Bands [12, 13, 14] contain no row: both outputs are NaN there (numpy: the mean of an empty slice, a RuntimeWarning, NaN) and NaN equals NaN in the comparison; every other band is finite. params.constants lists the module constants and the inline numbers the function reads (a port copies them from its own source and may assert that they equal these).
